lt-field.description: Wires label, field, help text and error text together: sets `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` on the control and an id on the help text and the error text. Never writes an id on the control: the template writes `for` and `id`, or wraps the field in the label. The field is invalid when the error text is there without `hidden`. Exists for markup from code that cannot call a builder function. When it can, in TypeScript, Kotlin or Java, use `lt.field()` or `Lt.field()` instead.

optional.description: The field is optional, and the label says so.

described-by.description: Extra ids to include in `aria-describedby`, separated by spaces.

label.description: The label. When it is outside the element, it is wired with `for` to the control's id.

control.description: The control the field wires: an `<input>`, `<textarea>` or `<select>` with its `<option>`s. `type="hidden"` does not count, and only the first one is wired. The template writes `for` on the label and `id` on the control, or wraps the control in the label.

help.description: The help text, which is read out together with the control.

error.description: The error text, which is shown and read out when the field is invalid.

removed.invalid: The field is invalid when the error text, `.lt-error-text`, is visible, or when the server has written `aria-invalid` on the control. In Datastar: `data-attr:hidden="!$invalid"` on the error text.
removed.required-marker: The required marker is `data-required` on `<label>`, and then shows without JavaScript too.
removed.control-id: Write `id` on the control and `for` on the label in the template. The component never writes an id on the control.

lt-tabs.description: Tab list. The tabs are links to the panels in an `.lt-tabs__list`, so without JavaScript the list is a table of contents; `role="tab"` on anything other than a link is not a tab. The component adds keyboard and focus handling, sets roles and wiring, gives each panel its tab's name, makes only the selected panel a tab stop, and hides the rest with `hidden="until-found"`, so find in page and links into a panel reach them. Each selection is written to the URL. It never writes an id on a tab or a panel. When the page loads, the selected tab is the one with `aria-selected` from the server, otherwise the one the URL points to, otherwise the first one not hidden with `hidden`. Under `server-controlled` the URL never selects.

server-controlled.description: The server decides which tab is selected. The component does not put the user's selection back after an update from the server, and the URL selects no tab. A click and find in page select the tab until the server responds.

activation.description: What the arrow keys do. By default they select the tab at once.

list.description: The tab list, a `<ul>` where each `<li>` gets `role="presentation"`. It needs a name, such as `aria-label`. When the server has written `role="tab"` on the links, the list can also hold other links.

tab.description: A tab: a link to its panel, `<a href="#attachments">`. The component writes `aria-controls` from `href`. `role="tab"` on something that is not a link is not a tab.

panel.description: The content of one tab, with the id the link points to. The panel has the same name as the tab: the heading at the top of the panel is the name when it says the same as the tab.

lt-error-summary.description: Error summary. Moves focus to the box when it appears, and to the control when a link in the list is followed.

data-autofocus.description: Whether focus moves to the box when it appears. On by default.

hidden.description: The box is hidden. The server removes the attribute when the form fails, and the component then moves focus.

title.description: The heading in the box. The component gives it the title class.

link.description: A link to a field with an error, in a list item. `href` is `#` and the field's id.

lt-popover.description: A panel that hangs from a button and closes itself. A button and a panel with the class `lt-popover` and an id from the template; the component sets `popover` and `aria-controls` where the markup came without them, but never the id.

open.description: The panel is open. The server can send the attribute to open the panel.

placement.description: Which edge of the button the panel hangs from.

server-controlled.description: The server decides whether the panel is open. The component does not put `open` back when an update from the server removes it.

trigger.description: The button that opens and closes the panel: the one with `aria-controls` pointing at the panel's id, otherwise the first button outside the panel.

panel.description: The panel that opens: the element with `popover`, or the class. It needs an id from the server, which `aria-controls` on the button points to. The component never creates one, and without it the button cannot be wired to the panel.

lt-term.description: A word in the text that shows its glossary entry in a card by the word. A link to the entry's id is enough; the component sets the class, `aria-details` and `aria-expanded` on the link, and shows the entry itself in the top layer while the card is open. Without JavaScript the word is a link to the glossary.

word.description: The word: a link to the glossary entry, such as `<a href="#term-signal">`. The entry is a `<div>` with that id in a `<dl>`, with a `<dt>` and a `<dd>`, anywhere on the page.

lt-suggestion.description: Field with a suggestion list. A `<label for>`, an `<input id>`, an `.lt-suggestion__list` with `<li>` items and a `[role=status]` are enough; the component sets the roles and the wiring where the markup came without them, and gives the list and the options ids. The field never gets an id from the component. Filters as the user types, moves the highlight with the arrow keys and announces the number of matches.

prefiltered.description: The app has already filtered the list, so the component leaves it as it is. Needed when the app's filter is something other than "the text contains the search term".

count-none.description: The announcement for no matches. The default is "No matches".

count-zero.description: The announcement in the plural form `zero`, for languages that have it. `{n}` is the number.

count-one.description: The announcement for one match. `{n}` is the number.

count-two.description: The announcement in the plural form `two`, for languages that have it. `{n}` is the number.

count-few.description: The announcement in the plural form `few`, for languages that have it. `{n}` is the number.

count-many.description: The announcement in the plural form `many`, for languages that have it. `{n}` is the number.

count-other.description: The announcement for every other count, and the fallback when a form is missing. `{n}` is the number.

server-controlled.description: The server decides whether the list is expanded and which option is highlighted. The component does not put them back after an update from the server.

control.description: The field the user types in: `role="combobox"`, otherwise the first `<input>`. The template writes `for` on the label and `id` on the field, or wraps the field in the label.

list.description: The list of suggestions. It sits in the top layer when it is open, `popover="manual"`, and has the label as its name.

option.description: One suggestion in the list: `role="option"`, or an `<li>` without a role.

empty.description: The message shown when nothing matches.

status.description: The announcement of the number of matches. The element is left empty, and the component fills it.

value.description: A hidden `<input>` that gets the `data-value` of the option the user chose. Without it, only the text in the field is submitted.

label.description: The label. The component writes `for` on it from the field's id when it does not wrap the field, and names the list after it.

lt-dialog.description: Makes a `<dialog class="lt-dialog">` the server sends open a real modal, with `showModal()`. The host around the dialog. Gives the dialog its name from the first heading outside `lt-dialog__body` when neither `aria-labelledby` nor `aria-label` is there.

open.description: The dialog is open. For the server to show it, `open` must be on `<dialog>` too.

server-controlled.description: When an update from the server removes `open` from `<dialog>` while the dialog is open, the component closes it and dispatches `dialog-toggle`, instead of putting `open` back.

dialog.description: The `<dialog>` element, as a direct child of the host.

title.description: The title: what `aria-labelledby` points to, otherwise the first heading outside the body. With `aria-label` on `<dialog>` it is not needed.

body.description: The body, which scrolls when the dialog gets too tall. A heading here does not become the title.

lt-toast.description: A queue of short messages in the corner of the screen. The messages are created from script with `show(text, { color, duration })`.

duration.description: Milliseconds before a message disappears. The default is 6000, and 0 keeps the messages.

label.description: Text that tells screen readers what the region is for.

close-label.description: What the close button in each message is called for screen readers. The default is "Close message".

lt-session-timeout.description: Warns before a signed-in session expires, and counts down. The renderer writes the dialog and the text inside the element: a `<dialog>` with `.lt-session-timeout__count` for the number, `[role=status]` for the announcement and the buttons in a `<form method="dialog">`. Dispatches `session-warn` when the dialog opens, `session-extend` when the user wants to continue, `session-logout` when the user logs out with a button that closes the dialog, `session-expired` when time is up, and `session-activity` at most once per `activity-interval` while the user is active, so the app can keep the server session alive.

warn-at.description: Seconds without activity before the warning appears.

expires-at.description: Seconds without activity before the session expires.

activity-interval.description: Seconds between each `session-activity` while the user is active. Default 60.

title.description: The heading in the dialog, which becomes its name when neither `aria-labelledby` nor `aria-label` is on `<dialog>`.

text.description: The paragraph with the time remaining. The announcement is this paragraph with the number replaced.

count.description: The number that counts down, inside the paragraph. The component fills it.

status.description: The announcement. The element is left empty, and the component fills it.

button.description: The buttons in `<form method="dialog">`, which extend the session or log out.

lt-connection-status.description: Tells the user when the connection to the server is lost. The app reports with `reportFailure()` and `reportSuccess()`.

offline-text.description: The text when the connection is lost.

online-text.description: The text when it comes back.

connectionOffline.text: No connection. What you type is not being saved.

builders.name: accordion
builders.description:
The attributes for a panel that can be expanded.

The class goes on a `<details>` with a `<summary>` first. The browser handles opening, closing, the keyboard and screen readers announcing "expanded" or "collapsed". Build the same thing from buttons and `aria-expanded`, and all of that must be written again, and the browser's find in page no longer finds text inside a closed panel.
builders.example:
Who can take out a policy?
…

options.name: variant
options.description: Its own frame, or just a line between the panels. Default: `default`.

builders.name: alert
builders.description:
The attributes for a message about the whole page or a whole form.

The role is not set here, because it depends on when the message comes. If it is in the markup from the start, it should have no role. If it appears while the page is idle, it needs `role="status"`, or `role="alert"` if the user must stop.
builders.example: Your routes have not been saved

options.description: What the message means. Left out, it is the neutral one.

The attributes for a profile picture or initials.

If the name is already next to it, the picture is decoration: set `aria-hidden="true"` on it, or the name is announced twice. If the picture stands alone, it must have a text that says who it is.

options.description: Size. Default: `medium`.

options.name: variant
options.description: Round or rounded square. Default: `circle`.

builders.name: breadcrumbs
builders.description:
The attributes for a breadcrumb trail.

The class goes on an `<ol>` inside a `<nav>` with a text that says what the navigation is, for example `aria-label="You are here"`. The order matters, so the list must be numbered even though the numbers are not shown.

The separator between the steps is added with CSS. Had it been in the markup, screen readers would have read "slash" between every step.
builders.example:
1. Home
  2. My claims

builders.name: button
builders.description: The attributes for a button.

options.name: variant
options.description: How weighty the action is. Default: `primary`.

builders.name: card
builders.description:
The attributes for a card.

`interactive` gives hover and a focus ring, but makes nothing clickable by itself. If the whole card should be pressable, the element must be an `<a>` or a `<button>`. A `<div>` with a click listener can neither be reached with the keyboard nor be announced as something to press.

options.name: variant
options.description: Surface or outline. Default: `outline`.

options.name: interactive
options.description: The whole card is clickable. Use only on `<a>` or `<button>`.

builders.name: checkbox
builders.description:
The attributes for a checkbox.

`type` is set here, so the box cannot become a text field with a box's styling. The indeterminate state is set with `element.indeterminate = true` in JavaScript, not as an attribute, because HTML has no such attribute.

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state. Default: `default`.

builders.name: connectionStatus
builders.description:
The attributes for the bar that says the connection is lost.

By definition the server cannot tell you it is unreachable. When it is down, nothing comes from it to render. So the component creates all the content itself, and `data-ignore-morph` stops a later patch from tearing it away the moment the connection is back. The host is the live region, `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so the region exists before the bar and its text arrive.

options.name: offlineText
options.description: The text when the connection is lost.

options.name: onlineText
options.description: The text when it comes back. Shown for a short while.

builders.name: dialog
builders.description:
The attributes for a dialog.

Opening a dialog is a call, not an attribute: only `showModal()` moves focus in, keeps focus inside the dialog, closes on Escape and makes the rest of the page inert. A `<dialog open>` in the markup is a box on the page.

That is a problem for a server that only sends HTML, since it cannot call anything in the browser. So the server says the dialog is open, and `<lt-dialog>` makes the call.

The two `open`s are not the same, and it is worth keeping them apart:

- `open` on the **host** is the server saying the dialog should be shown. It is not preserved. If it were, the server could never open the dialog again after the user had closed it once. If the server sends the region again with `open` still set, the dialog opens again. For a dismissal to last, the app must tell the server.
- `open` on the **`<dialog>`** is set by the browser itself when `showModal()` is called. It is not in the server's HTML, so a morph removes it, and the component puts it back. The server also writes it when it knows the dialog should be shown: without JavaScript a `<dialog>` without `open` is hidden, and its content does not exist for the reader. With the attribute it stands as a box on the page until the component turns it into a modal.
builders.example:
const box = lt.dialog({ titleId: "cancel-title", open: true })

Cancel job 222-0481?

The crew keeps the advance. This cannot be undone.

options.name: titleId
options.description: Id of the heading. The dialog takes its name from it with `aria-labelledby`. Make it from a key in the data, never from the loop index or a counter, so it is unique on the page and the same on every render.

options.name: open
options.description: The dialog is open. Default: closed.

options.name: color
options.description: Colour of the header. Default: `neutral`, which gives none.

builders.name: divider
builders.description:
The attributes for a divider.

The class goes on an `<hr>`. If the line separates two parts of the content, it is information screen readers should get. If it is only decoration between two boxes that are already apart, set `aria-hidden="true"` on it.

options.name: variant
options.description: How visible the line is. Default: `default`.

builders.name: errorSummary
builders.description:
The attributes for an error summary.

The server writes the whole box, including the heading and the list. `<lt-error-summary>` only moves focus and handles clicks on the links. The component used to create the heading itself, and then it disappeared on every morph in Datastar.
builders.example:
const summary = lt.errorSummary({ count: errors.length, id: "errors", titleId: "errors-title", })

You need to fix 2 errors

  • The fixer's address is missing an @

options.name: count
options.description: The number of errors the server found. When it is zero, the box is hidden.

options.name: id
options.description: The id of the box, so the form can move focus here after submission. Make it from a key in the data, never from the loop index or a counter, so it is unique on the page and the same on every render.

options.name: titleId
options.description: The id of the heading. The box takes its name from it with `aria-labelledby`. Default: the box's `id` with `-title`, so the markup carries the wiring whenever the box has an id. An empty one counts as none; one with whitespace throws.

builders.name: errorText
builders.description: The attributes for an error text below a field.

options.name: variant
options.description: Whether the error stops submission or only warns. Default: `error`.

builders.name: field
builders.description:
Connects the label, field, help text and error text.

The same calculation `<lt-field>` does in the browser, but as data, for the code that renders the markup. Then no web component is needed.
builders.example:
const field = lt.field({ id: "fixer", required: "text", help: true, error: true, invalid })

The board writes to the fixer, never to the crew.

Enter the fixer's address, for example fixer@relay.example.

options.name: id
options.description: The id of the control. Required. Make it from a key in the data, never from the loop index or a counter, so it is unique on the page and the same on every render.

options.name: help
options.description: The field has a help text to connect with `aria-describedby`.

options.name: error
options.description: The field has an error text. It is hidden until the field is invalid.

options.name: helpId
options.description: A separate id for the help text. Derived from `id` if left out.

options.name: errorId
options.description: A separate id for the error text. Derived from `id` if left out.

options.name: required
options.description: Marks the label as required.

options.name: optional
options.description: Marks the label as optional.

options.name: invalid
options.description: The field is invalid: shows the error text and sets `aria-invalid`.

options.name: disabled
options.description: The control is disabled.

options.name: describedBy
options.description: Extra ids to include in `aria-describedby`.

builders.name: fieldset
builders.description:
The attributes for a group of controls that belong together.

`<fieldset>` with `<legend>` is the one way to give a set of radio buttons or checkboxes a shared label that screen readers actually announce before each choice.

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state for the whole group. Default: `default`.

options.name: disabled
options.description: Disables all the controls in the group.

builders.name: fileUpload
builders.description:
The attributes for a file upload field.

The field is a plain `<input type="file">`. The button inside is the browser's own, and its text comes from the operating system's language. It cannot be translated, so the label above the field must say what to upload.

`accept` is a help in the file picker, not a barrier. The user can choose "all files", so the type must be checked on the server anyway.

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state. Default: `default`.

options.name: multiple
options.description: Allow several files.

options.name: accept
options.description: The file types the field accepts, such as `.pdf,image/*`.

builders.name: heading
builders.description:
The attributes for a heading.

Size and level are two different things. The level is `<h1>` to `<h6>` and sets the structure screen readers navigate by; `size` only sets how large the text looks. An `<h2>` that should look small is correct; an `<h4>` chosen because it was small enough skips a level in the structure.

options.name: size
options.description: Visual size. Default: `l`.

builders.name: helpText
builders.description: The attributes for help text below a field.

options.name: variant
options.description: How loudly the text should speak. Default: `muted`.

builders.name: icon
builders.description:
The attributes for an icon. The class goes on an `<svg>`, and the svg comes from the app's icon set: LO-TEK ships no icons.

The icon is as large as the text around it, and is drawn in the colour the svg says, which should be `currentColor`. Without `label` it is decoration, and if it stands alone in a button, the button must get its name somewhere else: `aria-label` on the button, or a text with `lt-sr-only`. The core reports a button that lacks one.

options.name: label
options.description: What the icon means, when it stands alone and means something, such as a warning sign with no text next to it. Becomes `aria-label` with `role="img"`. Without it the icon is decoration, and is hidden from screen readers.

builders.name: input
builders.description:
The attributes for a text field.

`type` sets both the HTML type and the icon variant, so the two cannot get out of step. Write them by hand, and it is easy to get a date field that looks like a date field, but where nothing happens when the user presses the icon.

options.name: type
options.description: The HTML type. Set as `type`, and decides the icon. Default: `text`.

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state. Default: `default`.

builders.name: label
builders.description:
The attributes for a label.

The marker is only visual, so set `required` on the field itself as well, or the screen reader is not told that it must be filled in.

options.name: required
options.description: Marks the field as required, with an asterisk or with the word "(required)".

options.name: optional
options.description: Marks the field as optional. Choose one of `required` and `optional`.

options.name: disabled
options.description: Mutes the text when the control is disabled.

builders.name: legend
builders.description:
The attributes for the label of a group.

The same marker as `label()`, but on a `<legend>`.

options.name: required
options.description: Marks the group as required, with an asterisk or with the word "(required)".

options.name: optional
options.description: Marks the group as optional. Choose one of `required` and `optional`.

options.name: disabled
options.description: Mutes the text when the group is disabled.

builders.name: link
builders.description:
The attributes for a link.

An `<a>` without `href` is no link to a screen reader and is not in the tab order. `role` and `tabindex` give it both back while it is disabled.
builders.example: Read the small print See annual statement

options.name: disabled
options.description: The link cannot be clicked yet. Gives `aria-disabled`, `role="link"` and `tabindex="0"`, so screen readers still find it as a link and can say so. Remove `href` as well: otherwise Enter follows it.

builders.name: list
builders.description:
The attributes for a list.

The class goes on `<ul>` or `<ol>`. `plain` and `divided` remove the bullets visually, but the list stays a list, so the screen reader still says how many items it has. That is why the variant exists: without it people would use `<div>` to get rid of the bullets. The exception is Safari, where a `<ul>` without visible bullets can need `role="list"`. See the component page.

options.name: variant
options.description: Bullets, plain rows, or rows with a line between them. Default: `default`.

builders.name: pagination
builders.description:
The attributes for pagination.

The class goes on a `<ul>` inside a `<nav aria-label="Pagination">`. Each page is a link with its own address, not a button: the user can then open page three in a new tab, and come back with the back button.

The current page is marked with `aria-current="page"`, which both gives the colour and is what the screen reader announces.

builders.name: paragraph
builders.description:
The attributes for a paragraph.

The width is limited to 70 characters. Longer lines make it hard to find the start of the next one, and that is the most common reason a text is hard to read even when the type is large enough.
builders.example: A short summary of what the page is about.

options.name: size
options.description: Text size. Default: `medium`.

options.name: variant
options.description: `lead` is the introduction right below the heading. Default: `default`.

builders.name: popover
builders.description:
The attributes for a popover.

The server writes both the button and the panel, with the wiring between them. `<lt-popover>` works out the position and closes on a click outside.
builders.example:
const box = lt.popover({ id: "help" })
EB 100 a night past the return date. No exceptions.

options.name: id
options.description: Id of the panel. Connects the button to the panel with `aria-controls`. Make it from a key in the data, never from the loop index or a counter, so it is unique on the page and the same on every render.

options.name: open
options.description: The panel is open. Default: closed.

options.name: placement
options.description: Which edge the panel hangs from. Default: `bottom-start`.

builders.name: progress
builders.description:
The attributes for a progress bar on a `<progress>`.

The element has the semantics built in: the browser exposes it as `role="progressbar"` and announces how far it has come. You need neither a role, `aria-valuenow` nor `aria-valuemax`.

Leave out `value`, and the bar becomes indeterminate: "something is going on, we do not know for how long". That is the same as `lt.spinner()` says, so choose one of them.

`max` defaults to 100 and is always written out, against the rule that a default gives no attribute. The reason is that the rule is about appearance, where the CSS already has the answer. `max` is semantics, and HTML's own default is `1`: a `<progress value="40">` without `max` shows a full bar, without anything saying so.

options.name: value
options.description: How far it has come. Leave it out, and the bar is indeterminate.

options.name: max
options.description: What counts as full. Default: `100`.

options.name: color
options.description: What the number means. The default is the accent colour, meaning "this is in progress".

options.name: label
options.description: What is in progress. Becomes `aria-label`, so the bar has a name.

options.name: valueText
options.description: How far it has come, in words. Becomes `aria-valuetext`, which the screen reader reads instead of the percentage: "Step 3 of 7" says more than "43 percent", and `max` is rarely announced.

builders.name: radio
builders.description:
The attributes for a radio button.

All the buttons in a group must have the same `name`. That connection is what lets only one be selected, and lets the arrow keys move between them. You set `name` yourself, since only you know what the group is called.

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state. Default: `default`.

builders.name: search
builders.description:
The attributes for a search field.

The field is an `lt-input` with room for the magnifying glass, so both classes are set. `type="search"` gives the browser's own cross for clearing the field, and on mobile a keyboard with "Search" instead of "Enter".

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state. Default: `default`.

builders.name: select
builders.description: The attributes for a dropdown list.

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state. Default: `default`.

options.name: picker
options.description: Who draws the dropdown list. Default: `auto`.

builders.name: sessionTimeout
builders.description:
The attributes for the warning that a signed-in session is about to expire.

The renderer writes the dialog and all of the text, in its own language and with its own translation tool. The component only keeps time: it opens and closes the dialog, fills in the number and announces the countdown.

The buttons are plain buttons in a `<form method="dialog">`. The browser closes the dialog and sets `returnValue` to the button's `value`, and the component reads it. `data-ignore-morph` asks Datastar's morph to leave the warning alone. Without it the morph takes `open` and the number while the dialog is in the top layer. The component puts `open` back, and the number comes back on the next tick. With the attribute the number stays the whole time.
builders.example:
const session = lt.sessionTimeout({ titleId: "session-title" })

Your session is ending

Your session on the Lattice ends in . Unsaved routes will be lost.

options.name: titleId
options.description: Id of the heading. The dialog takes its name from it with `aria-labelledby`. Make it from a key in the data, never from the loop index or a counter, so it is unique on the page and the same on every render.

options.name: warnAt
options.description: Seconds without activity before the warning appears. Default: 25 minutes.

options.name: expiresAt
options.description: Seconds without activity before the session expires. Default: 30 minutes.

options.name: activityInterval
options.description: Seconds between each `session-activity` while the user is active. Default: 60.

builders.name: skeleton
builders.description:
The attributes for a placeholder while the content loads.

The shapes are always hidden from screen readers. They say nothing about what is coming, and a row of empty boxes being announced is worse than silence. Announce the wait in one place instead, with `role="status"`.

options.name: variant
options.description: Shape. Default: `block`.

builders.name: skipLink
builders.description:
The attributes for a skip-to-content link.

The link must be the first element in `<body>`, and point to the id of the main content. It sits off screen until it gets focus, and therefore cannot be hidden with `display: none`: the keyboard could not reach it either, and the whole point is lost.

builders.name: spinner
builders.description:
The attributes for a loading indicator.

Without `label` the ring is only a shape, and is hidden from screen readers with `aria-hidden`, as an icon without a label is. With `label` it becomes a `role="status"` that says what is going on. If you already have a visible text next to it, let that carry the message and drop `label`, so the same thing is not announced twice.

options.name: size
options.description: Size. Default: `medium`.

options.name: label
options.description: What is loading. Becomes `aria-label`, so the ring has a name for screen readers.

builders.name: srOnly
builders.description:
The attributes for text that only screen readers should get.

Use it when a label or explanation is needed by someone listening to the page, but would be noise to someone looking at it. If the content should be gone for everyone, use `hidden` instead.

builders.name: steps
builders.description:
The attributes for a step indicator, which shows where the user is in a task over several pages, like an order.

The class goes on an `<ol>` with one `<li>` per step, and the step the user is on has `aria-current="step"`. The steps before it are drawn as done, with a check the screen reader reads as "Completed", so the markup only says where the user is. A done step can be a link back to it.

builders.name: suggestion
builders.description:
The attributes for a field with a suggestion list.

The server writes both the field and the list. The web component filters, handles the arrow keys and keeps `aria-activedescendant` in sync. It renders nothing: it used to create the whole field itself, and then there was nothing to fill in before the script had run.

No preserve list. The attributes that change while the user types are set by the web component, and it sets them back when a patch strips them. If something else has already filtered, set `prefiltered` on `<lt-suggestion>`, and the web component leaves both the options and the empty message alone. If the server should also decide whether the list is expanded and which option is highlighted, set `server-controlled` as well.

options.name: invalid
options.description: The field is invalid: shows the error text and sets `aria-invalid`.

options.name: error
options.description: The field has an error text. It is hidden until the field is invalid.

options.name: disabled
options.description: The control is disabled.

options.name: required
options.description: Marks the label as required.

options.name: optional
options.description: Marks the label as optional.

options.name: help
options.description: The field has a help text to connect with `aria-describedby`.

options.name: helpId
options.description: A separate id for the help text. Derived from `id` if left out.

options.name: errorId
options.description: A separate id for the error text. Derived from `id` if left out.

options.name: describedBy
options.description: Extra ids to include in `aria-describedby`.

options.name: id
options.description: Shared id stem. The control becomes `${id}`, the list `${id}-list`, and the options `${id}-option-${key}`. Make it from a key in the data, never from the loop index or a counter, so it is unique on the page and the same on every render.

options.name: keys
options.description: One key per option the server sends, taken from the data, such as a record id. The key gives the option its id, so an update that sends the list again recognises the options. An empty key, whitespace or two identical keys throw. Default: no options.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The option highlighted with the arrow keys. Default: none.

options.name: open
options.description: The list is open. Default: closed.

options.name: pending
options.description: The answer to the search has not arrived yet. The list gets `aria-busy`, and the empty message stays hidden, so an asynchronous search does not say "No matches" in the gap between the keystroke and the answer.

builders.name: switch
builders.description:
The attributes for an on/off switch.

The switch is a checkbox with `role="switch"`. Screen readers then announce it as "on" and "off" rather than "checked", while the keyboard and `FormData` work as for a plain checkbox.

The switch has no validation state. A choice that is on or off cannot be invalid in itself; if turning it on is required, the requirement belongs in a checkbox with `required`.

options.name: disabled
options.description: The control is disabled. Do not use it to lock the switch while a save is in progress: `disabled` takes focus away from it, and focus does not come back.

builders.name: table
builders.description:
The attributes for a table.

The class goes on a real `<table>` with `<thead>` and `<th>`. The header cells are what let screen readers say "Amount, 1,240 kroner" when the user is in a cell. Build the table from `<div>` elements, and that connection does not exist.

options.name: variant
options.description: Every other row on a muted surface. Default: `default`.

options.name: hoverable
options.description: Highlights the row under the mouse. Use only when rows can be pressed.

builders.name: tableSort
builders.description:
The attributes for a sortable column header.

`aria-sort` is on the `<th>`, not on the button, because the cell is what describes the column. Only the sorted column has the attribute. The arrow is drawn from the same attribute, so what the screen reader says and what is shown cannot drift apart. The sorting itself is the app's job.

options.name: direction
options.description: The direction the column is sorted in. Left out, it means the table is not sorted by this column, and the header gets no `aria-sort`.

builders.name: tabs
builders.description:
The attributes for a tab list where the tabs are links to the panels.

Only links, ids and classes. Without JavaScript the tab list is then a plain list of links, and the panels follow one another: a table of contents that works for everyone. The roles, which tab is selected and which panels are hidden are written by `<lt-tabs>`. Had they been here, the markup without JavaScript would have said "tab" about a link that does not behave like one, and hidden the panels.

The first tab is selected when the page loads. Another one comes from the address, such as `#file-attachments`, or from `selected` and `select()` on `<lt-tabs>`.
builders.example: const tabs = lt.tabs({ id: "file", keys: ["claim", "attachments"], label: "Parts of the claim" })

options.name: id
options.description: The shared id stem. The panels become `${id}-${key}`, and the headings in them `${id}-${key}-heading`. Make it from a key in the data, never from the loop index or a counter, so it is unique on the page and the same on every render.

options.name: keys
options.description: One key per tab, from the data, such as `["claim", "attachments"]`. The key gives the panel its id, and the link points to it. An index is not a key: if the server inserts a tab first, the same index points to another panel. An empty key, whitespace and two identical keys throw.

options.name: label
options.description: What the tabs choose between. Becomes `aria-label` on the tab list, which must have a name. Empty, or only whitespace, throws.

builders.name: tag
builders.description:
The attributes for a tag.

A tag labels content: keywords on an article, selected filters above a list. If it says what state something is in, Badge is right instead.

`selectable` gives hover and a focus ring, but makes nothing pressable. The element must be a `<button>`, and you set `aria-pressed` yourself, since only you know whether the tag is selected.

options.name: variant
options.description: Outline or muted surface. Default: `outline`.

options.name: selectable
options.description: The tag can be toggled on and off. Use only on a `<button>`.

builders.name: term
builders.description:
The attributes for a word in the text that is explained in a glossary on the same page.

Only what holds without JavaScript: the word is a link to the entry, and `aria-details` says the entry explains it. `<lt-term>` around the link opens the entry as a card by the word, and writes `aria-expanded`.
builders.example:
const signal = lt.term({ id: "term-signal" })

Datastar keeps signals in the browser.

Signal
A value Datastar keeps in the browser.

options.name: id
options.description: Id of the entry in the glossary: the `<div>` around the `<dt>` and `<dd>`. The word links to it, and the web component shows the entry itself as the card. Make it from the term, such as `term-signal`, so it is the same on every render.

builders.name: textarea
builders.description: The attributes for a multi-line text field.

options.name: state
options.description: Validation state. Default: `default`.

builders.name: toast
builders.description:
The attributes for the toast region.

The region is `role="status"` and not `role="alert"`. A message that comes because something went well should not interrupt what the screen reader is doing.

`data-ignore-morph` is not optional. `<lt-toast>` creates and removes its message elements inside the region, and without the attribute the Datastar morph tears them away at the next patch, because the server's version of the region is empty. The attribute must be in the HTML the server sends: the component cannot set it on itself, since the morph reads it from the server's node.

options.name: label
options.description: Text that says what the region is. Becomes `aria-label`.

options.name: closeLabel
options.description: The screen reader name of the close button in each message. Default: "Close message". `closeLabel` in `show()` overrides it for one message.

builders.name: toggleGroup
builders.description:
The attributes for a group where one option is selected at a time.

The group is radio buttons in disguise. Each option is a `<label>` with an `<input type="radio">` inside, visually shrunk away. You then keep the arrow keys, `FormData` and the screen reader saying "2 of 3" without writing any of it again.

If the choices are actions rather than a setting, such as "bold, italic, underline", buttons with `aria-pressed` belong there instead.
builders.example:
<fieldset {...toggleGroup()}>
  <legend class="lt-sr-only">View</legend>
  <label class={toggleGroup.option}>
    <input type="radio" name="view" value="dry" checked /> Dry
  </label>
</fieldset>

builders.name: tooltip
builders.description:
The attributes for the wrapper around a trigger and a tooltip bubble.

The bubble shows on hover and on focus. The focus part is not optional: a bubble that only comes with the mouse does not exist for keyboard users.

The text in the bubble must be connected to the trigger with `aria-describedby`. Without it the bubble is just something that appears on screen, and is never announced.

Use it for something extra, never for something the user must have. On a touch screen there is neither hover nor focus before something is tapped.
builders.example: At street value

families.accent: Links, primary button, focus, selected state
families.brand1: First brand colour: surfaces, sections and categories. Carries no meaning of its own
families.brand2: Second brand colour: surfaces, sections and categories. Carries no meaning of its own
families.brand3: Third brand colour: surfaces, sections and categories. Carries no meaning of its own

roles.surface: Tinted surface: a badge, an alert, a section
roles.border-subtle: Decorative line, such as between two rows
roles.border: The border around a field or a surface
roles.border-strong: The field border on hover, and a table line
roles.fill: Filled surface: a button, a checked checkbox
